title: Omni Tracker

hero.about: OmniGreen’s marketing team plans, ships and reports campaigns for several retail brands at once. I designed and built Omni Tracker as two products on one platform: an Admin panel where the team runs every campaign, and a Client mode where each brand sees its own live results, on brand and locked to its own data. Concept to production in three days.

modules.name: 01 Hero
heading: Omni Tracker is
one home for every
campaign we run
text:
Project_ Omni Tracker
Designed and built by_ Vignesh Murali

OmniGreen’s marketing team plans, ships and reports campaigns for several retail brands at once. I designed and built Omni Tracker as two products on one platform: an Admin panel where the team runs every campaign, and a Client mode where each brand sees its own live results, on brand and locked to its own data. Concept to production in three days.
modules.alt: Hero for Omni Tracker: the headline “Omni Tracker is one home for every campaign we run” above a laptop showing the Admin board for Beta Brand, with an About paragraph on the two products built in three days.

modules.name: 02 At a glance
heading: Two products.
One source of truth.
Three days.
modules.lede: Omni Tracker replaced a spreadsheet per brand, a separate BI tool and hand-built client reports with one shared workspace. The team works in Admin; every brand gets its own live page.
text: Omni Tracker replaced a spreadsheet per brand, a separate BI tool and hand-built client reports with one shared workspace. The team works in Admin; every brand gets its own live page.
For the OmniGreen team. Board, list, timeline and calendar for every brand; journeys; live Performance dashboards; Google Sheets two-way sync; comments with @mentions.
For each brand. A private, on-brand page with what is live, what is next and what it earned: North Star first, calendar, journeys, Creative and Web analytics.
modules.alt: At a glance: two products, one source of truth, three days, with eight stats (3 days, 2 products, 32 releases, 106 tests, 11 views, 6 tabs, 8 services, $0 infrastructure) and cards for the Admin panel and Client mode.

modules.name: 03 Problem
heading: Plans in Sheets.
Numbers in Metabase.
Reports by hand.
modules.lede: Every brand’s campaign plan lived in its own Google Sheet. Results sat in Metabase and Google Analytics, creative in Miro and Figma, and client updates were rebuilt by hand. Nobody could answer “what’s live this week, and is it working?” from one place.
text: Every brand’s campaign plan lived in its own Google Sheet. Results sat in Metabase and Google Analytics, creative in Miro and Figma, and client updates were rebuilt by hand. Nobody could answer “what’s live this week, and is it working?” from one place.
A Sheet per brand, kept up to date by hand
Results live in a different tool from the plan
No single answer to what is live and how it is doing
Every brand’s plan on one board, still synced both ways with its Sheet
Live Metabase numbers right beside the campaigns
Each brand gets a private page that updates itself
Comments, @mentions and an Inbox, in context
Same people, same Sheets, same data: one place to see it, and a safe way to share it.
modules.alt: The problem: a before diagram of a scattered stack (Sheets, Metabase, GA, Miro, hand-built client updates) compared with one Omni Tracker workspace that connects board, journeys, performance, creative, web analytics and Client mode.

modules.name: 04 Problem and solution
heading: Two audiences.
Two products.
One workspace.
text: Campaigns tracked in a Sheet per brand
→  One board, list, timeline and calendar for every brand, synced both ways with the same Sheets
→  A live page per brand: what is live, what is next, what it earned
Sharing a BI tool risks other clients’ data
→  Journeys as first-class objects: steps, triggers, offers, one Sheet tab each
→  Per-client sealed links; keys and queries never leave the server
Results in a separate BI tool
→  Live Metabase metrics, SQL charts and a customizable Performance page
→  On-brand OmniGreen UI with North Star Metrics first and full width
→  Comments with @mentions, an Inbox and email, on the campaign itself
→  Every chart downloads as an image or CSV; journey log and reports too
modules.alt: Problem and solution in two columns: the Admin panel for the team and Client mode for each brand, each listing old pains and how Omni Tracker answers them.

modules.lede: Every change shipped as its own pull request, tested and deployed to Vercel the same hour. The team used the tool while it was being built, and their feedback set the next release.
text: Every change shipped as its own pull request, tested and deployed to Vercel the same hour. The team used the tool while it was being built, and their feedback set the next release.

Download any chart as PNG or CSV, plus reports
Two-way Google Sheets sync, one tab per journey
Admin and Client mode split; short client links
Security review of the client link, then hardening
Journeys with steps, triggers and offers
Customizable dashboards: drag, resize, add, remove
Live Metabase metrics and SQL charts
Web analytics tab; clickable links in comments
Sign-in for the team and one shared workspace on Upstash
A private client page per brand, with its own key
@mentions with Inbox and email; edit and delete

modules.name: 11 Private links
heading: A link you can share
without sharing
a single secret.
modules.lede: Client mode had to be safe to forward. I reviewed it like an attacker would, then fixed what I found before anyone asked.
text: Client mode had to be safe to forward. I reviewed it like an attacker would, then fixed what I found before anyone asked.
Admin turns the brand’s settings into a short link: /c/brand/id
Settings are encrypted with AES-256-GCM using the access key and a server secret
The client types the key; it never goes in the URL. 10 wrong tries locks it for 15 minutes
Sheets and Metabase are read with keys that live only in Vercel
The page gets chart-ready rows for that brand, nothing more
SECURITY REVIEW OF THE LIVE CLIENT LINK
No API keys or queries in the client page or its code
Every Admin API answers 401 without a team sign-in
10 wrong keys from one address, then a 15 minute wait
Outbound calls refuse private and internal addresses
Headers stop clickjacking and content sniffing
Clients see a friendly message; details stay in server logs
modules.alt: Private links: a five-step flow from making a link to sending only what is allowed, and a security review of the live client link with six checks.

modules.name: 14 Hard problems
heading: Four problems
that shaped
the product.
modules.lede: Shipping daily means finding problems early. These four changed how the tool works under the hood.
text: Shipping daily means finding problems early. These four changed how the tool works under the hood.
A card deleted in the app reappeared minutes later: the sheet sync re-added the row before the sheet had caught up.
The security release added one more server endpoint. Vercel’s free plan allows twelve, so production stayed on the old build.
Deletions now leave a tombstone, so deletions always win; the sync keeps retrying the sheet delete. A test with a fake sheet reproduces the old bug.
The endpoint folded into an existing one, and a test now fails if the app ever needs more than twelve.
The North Star report was deleted from a brand, and nothing could bring it back: not seeding, not Customize.
The Metabase question picker opened clipped inside its card: frosted glass traps fixed pop-ups.
A one-time restore put it back on top, and Customize now lists removed team reports so one click undoes it.
Pop-ups and modals now render above the whole page, and a broken chart shows a message instead of a blank app.
modules.alt: What went wrong: four problems with their fixes: deleted cards came back, a deploy that quietly failed, a chart lost by accident, and menus trapped under glass.

modules.name: 16 Learnings and next
heading: What I learned,
and what
comes next.
text: Ship to the people who use it, daily
Screenshots from the team were the best spec. Every release answered one of them.
Top five products and categories per brand, from the order data.
GA4 charts drawn in the app, with names and downloads like every other chart.
Sheets stayed the source of truth, so adoption needed no training.
The Grok bot for CleverTap over MCP, in Admin only.
A client link is a public door. Treat it like one from day one.
Verify the domain so @mentions reach everyone’s inbox.
modules.alt: Reflection: three learnings and four next steps (best sellers, native web analytics, CRM agent, email on the team domain).
